headline: Lake Pend Oreille and Schweitzer Seasonal Access
reservation: No permits are required for town access or hiking, but Schweitzer Mountain activities and City Beach moorings have separate fees. Accommodations for the Festival at Sandpoint or peak ski weeks require booking months in advance. Check the official Idaho Parks and Recreation site for boat launch status.

days.title: Lakefront and Local Life

stops.name: Sandpoint City Beach
stops.detail: Stroll the sandy peninsula for views of the Selkirk and Cabinet Mountains across the water.

stops.name: Cedar Street Bridge Public Market
stops.detail: Browse local artisan shops in this unique bridge-based market spanning Sand Creek.

days.driving: Minimal; most town sites are walkable or a 5-minute local transfer.
days.note: City Beach is most active during summer months; lake temperatures remain brisk until July.

days.title: Alpine Summits and Selkirk Vistas

stops.name: Schweitzer Mountain Resort
stops.detail: Take the chairlift (seasonal) for 360-degree views stretching into Canada and Montana.

stops.name: Mickinnick Trail
stops.detail: Hike through dense cedar forests to reach high-altitude overlooks of the entire lake basin.

days.driving: Allow 30–45 minutes for the winding mountain ascent; check for winter road requirements.
days.note: This is active bear country; carry bear spray and stay on marked forest trails.

days.title: Shoreline Trails and Scenic Drives

stops.name: Pend Oreille Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive east toward Hope to see the Clark Fork Delta and rugged shoreline cliffs.

stops.name: Mineral Point Trail
stops.detail: Enjoy an easier forest walk with access to quiet, rocky beaches along the lake’s edge.

days.driving: Allow 1.5–2 hours for the scenic loop; roads are paved but narrow in sections.
days.note: The Clark Fork Delta area is a prime spot for bald eagle and osprey viewing.

intel.title: Downtown and Beach
intel.text: City Beach parking is limited during summer weekends and local festivals. Utilize downtown street parking and use the pedestrian paths if the main lot is full.

intel.title: Mountain Shadows
intel.text: Signal is strong in town but drops quickly on the Mickinnick Trail and remote sections of the Scenic Byway. Carry a physical map for backcountry forest roads.

intel.title: Regional Hub
intel.text: Sandpoint is the primary service hub for the northern Panhandle. Ensure you fuel up here before heading north toward the Canadian border.

intel.title: Schweitzer Seasons
intel.text: The resort transitions between ski operations and summer hiking/biking; check their official calendar for 'shoulder season' closures in spring and fall.

intel.title: Water Safety
intel.text: Lake Pend Oreille is exceptionally deep and can produce sudden large swells. Check marine forecasts at the marina before taking small watercraft far from shore.

plan.arrival: Fly into Spokane (GEG), rent a vehicle, and take the 90-minute scenic drive north through Coeur d'Alene to Sandpoint.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for summer, but a 4WD vehicle with winter tires is necessary for Schweitzer access during ski season.
plan.goldenHour: The Long Bridge pedestrian path offers unobstructed western views over the water, best during late summer evenings.
